chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from one of our companions, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from Bakr ibn Muhammad, from Aysama, who said:

I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and his wives were with him. He said, 'He smelled the scent of the perfume container,' and asked, 'What is this?' They said, 'It is a perfume container in which the hair oil (safflower oil) is placed.' He said, 'Order it to be poured out into the gutter.'

key_terms.الصَّيَّاح: A specific type of oil or perfume, often identified as safflower oil used for hair
key_terms.النَّضُوح: Perfume container or vessel for scent

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the perfume or oil known as 'al-sayyah' in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Note: The narrator is Abu Abdullah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), not Ali ibn Abi Talib. This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the practical application of ritual purity laws, where Imam al-Sadiq (as) discarded 'al-sayyah'—a fragrant oil or perfume used by women—into the gutter, signaling its status as *najis* (impure) or requiring specific handling. This incident highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on distinguishing between general cleanliness and ritual purity in daily life, particularly regarding substances used for adornment.
